Revision checklist before you close this book
Can you say, in one breath: design in the cloud, run on the runtime, push documents through shapes, package to deploy, extensions per environment, Process Reporting to troubleshoot?
Can you explain connector vs connection vs operation, document vs record, and DDP vs DPP without notes?
Have you built the CSV-to-JSON assignment, broken it on purpose, and read the error?
Can you name three BW 5.x comparisons with the right level (Direct, Similar, Partial, None)?
Have you checked every VERIFY item against help.boomi.com for your AtomSphere version?
FINAL TIP Build something every day. Reading alone will not make you confident. You already know how failures look in production; that is an advantage worth presenting.
End of book. Prepared for Ravi Raya.

cert01.text: A practical, scenario-led companion to the preserved Integration Essentials

Keep the original theory chapters and all 20 original course activities as the primary source book. This supplement adds a certification-oriented learning path, concept comparisons, additional practical drills, troubleshooting scenarios, mock examinations and readiness scoring. The original source pages have not been retyped or rewritten.

Exam-information caution: Boomi publicly describes the Associate Integration Developer course as covering complex process creation, the development lifecycle, document flow, properties and developer administration tools. Public official pages reviewed for this edition did not provide a stable, detailed public exam blueprint, current question count, passing score or time limit. Those details are therefore not guessed. Check the logged-in Boomi Training and Certification portal immediately before booking.

Scope discipline: The goal is associate-level process development. Learn advanced platform features only to the extent they help explain core process behavior; do not substitute architect-level design study for hands-on process building.

The current official Boomi training page recommends starting with Getting Started with the Boomi Platform and Integration Essentials, then lists Associate Integration Developer as a course. Boomi describes the course as learning to create complex processes and understand the development lifecycle, document flow, properties and developer administration tools.

head: Evidence category
What this book treats as reliable
rows: Complex process creation; development lifecycle; document flow; properties; developer administration tools.
Official documentation used for technical explanations
Process building, components, profiles, connectors, process testing, extensions and Process Reporting.
Connector setup, mapping, properties, document behavior, logic shapes, testing, deployment and monitoring, with practical tasks.
Not publicly confirmed in sources reviewed
Current exam question count, passing score, duration, exact weighting, question distribution or whether a live practical assessment is currently included.

cert01.text: The original Activity Guide contains 20 sequential exercises that cover folders, Process Library installation, environments, runtime clouds, FTP and Disk connectors, Set Properties, testing, XML and flat-file profiles, mapping, default values, packaging, deployment, manual execution and undeployment. These are preserved in the source portion of this book and should be completed in order.

cert02.text: A process is a reusable component containing connected steps. A runtime executes a deployed process. Connector steps bring data into or send data out of a process. Documents move between steps. Profiles describe the shape of structured data. Maps transform a source structure into a target structure. Logic steps control the path. Testing, reporting and deployment validate and operate the solution.

head: Layer
Question to ask
Typical Boomi object
rows: How do I reach the endpoint?
What does the payload look like?
How do source fields become target fields?
Which version runs in which environment?
Did it run, and what failed?

cert02.text: The connector chain: do not confuse the three

head: Term
Meaning
Example
rows: Adapter type for a technology or application
Disk, FTP, SFTP, Database, Salesforce, HTTP Client
Host, port, URL, credentials, database name
Get a file, Send a file, Query Accounts, Create Customer
The process step that uses the selected connection and operation
Start step reads from FTP; later connector sends to ERP

cert02.text: Memory cue: Connector = which system/technology; Connection = where and as whom; Operation = what action.

Boomi components are reusable configuration objects in the Component Explorer. A connection or profile may be referenced by multiple processes. Changing a shared component can affect every process that uses it. Before editing or deleting a component, inspect dependencies and consider whether a new version or separate component is safer.

A nightly customer integration reads a CSV from SFTP, validates required fields, maps it to an ERP JSON structure, and sends each customer. The SFTP connector identifies the protocol; the connection stores host and authentication settings; the operation defines the directory and file selection; a flat-file profile describes the columns; the Map transforms the document; the ERP connector sends the target structure.

cert03.text: A Boomi document is the unit of data passed between process steps. It can represent a file, message, record or other payload. Do not assume one inbound file always equals one business record: a file may contain multiple records, and processing steps can split, combine or otherwise alter document flow.
An inbound connector retrieves data and creates one or more documents.
Each step receives documents on its incoming path and may preserve, transform, split, route or fail them.
A Map transforms document content from a source profile to a destination profile; the output remains a document.
A Decision routes a document according to a condition; Branch sends documents down multiple paths.
A connector send operation attempts delivery using the configured connection and operation.
Execution results and available document details can be reviewed in Process Reporting for deployed executions, subject to retention and tracking configuration.

head: Property type
Typical purpose
Scope / caution
rows: Carry a value with a particular document through a process
Document-specific; useful for per-record context and connector attributes.
Store a runtime value for process logic or later steps
Process execution scope; not the same as a document-specific value.
Reusable configured values for a process
Component configuration; can be extended where supported.
Set connector-specific metadata such as file name, directory or mail subject
Use the correct connector property in Set Properties; it may affect connector behavior.

cert03.text: Important: Property names and availability vary by step and connector. Confirm the property type in the Set Properties configuration. Do not assume a value set on one document is automatically shared with all other documents.

If a process returns fewer documents than expected, check: inbound operation filters; whether the input contains multiple records; any split/merge or Data Process step; Decision conditions; Branch paths; map errors; connector response behavior; and document-level error handling.

One file contains 100 customer rows. A process produces 100 output documents after a split. One row fails validation. What should you inspect? First identify the step where document count changes; inspect the failed document and its source row; confirm whether the design intentionally routes invalid rows to a reject path; and verify that the other 99 documents continue as intended.

cert04.text: 3. Profiles, maps and transformation
Profiles describe structure; maps transform content

A profile describes the layout or format of data, including elements, fields, data types and file-specific structure. A Map uses a source profile and a destination profile to define field-level transformation. The profile is not the transformation itself.

head: Profile type
Common use
Things to verify
rows: Element hierarchy, namespaces, attributes, repeating elements, data types
Object/array nesting, field names, data types, optional values
Delimiter, qualifier, header, field order, lengths, record layout
Column names, types, nullable fields, imported schema

cert04.text: Map build sequence
Confirm the exact source and destination structures from representative payloads or imported schemas.
Create or import source and destination profiles.
Create a Map component and choose source and destination profiles.
Map like-for-like fields first; then add functions for formatting, concatenation, lookup, conversion or conditional logic as required.
Configure defaults deliberately and decide how null, empty and missing values should behave.
Test with typical, boundary and invalid data; inspect the actual output document.
Re-test after profile changes because profile re-imports can affect dependent maps.
Null, empty and missing are not interchangeable

head: Input condition
Possible meaning
Design decision
rows: Source did not provide the element/key
Use default, reject, or leave target absent
Preserve null, default, or reject according to target contract
Field exists but contains no characters
Trim, default, or preserve empty string
Value may look blank but contain spaces
Value cannot be converted to target type
Reject or route to an error path

cert04.text: Example: if a target requires Status and the source omits it, a default value such as ACTIVE may be appropriate only if the business rule explicitly says so. A default is not a substitute for understanding the target contract.
Common mapping defects
Wrong destination profile or operation request profile.
Source profile does not match the actual payload.
Array/repeating-element structure is mapped as a single value.
Date, number or Boolean conversion assumes the wrong format or locale.
A default is configured on the wrong target field or is applied even when a meaningful source value exists.
A profile was re-imported and changed element paths used by a map.

head: Step / shape
Use it for
Typical caution
rows: Check connector, filters and operation first.
Ensure all intended paths terminate appropriately.
Get or send data to an external system
Connection and operation must match the data and endpoint.
Input and output profiles must match actual payloads.
Choose the correct property type and scope.
Create text using static and dynamic content
Avoid exposing secrets or sensitive payloads in logs.
Do not assume test mode sends subscriber email alerts.
Perform supported document manipulation such as split or other configured processing
Confirm the resulting document count and content.
Choose a path based on a condition (true/false)
A condition routes; it does not duplicate the document.
Think fan-out; ensure downstream paths are safe and intentional.
Raise or handle an exception according to the configured step
Do not swallow failures without recording and action.
Catch and handle errors on supported editions/configurations
Confirm availability and actual retry behavior for your account.

cert05.text: Decision: one conditional choice, commonly true or false. Example: if CustomerEmail is empty, route to Reject; otherwise continue to ERP.
Branch: fan-out to multiple paths. Example: send a new employee record to Payroll, Identity Management and Facilities paths.
A common scenario trap is choosing Branch when only one mutually exclusive route is required, or choosing Decision when the same document must be sent to multiple destinations.

Error handling should preserve evidence and make recovery explicit. A Catch path can log context, notify support, route a failed document or perform a controlled recovery. A successful process status must not be used to hide a failed business transaction. Confirm feature availability in the account edition and the current product documentation.

head: Mechanism
Best fit
Key distinction
rows: Reusable configured value such as a business constant
Configured as a process property component.
Runtime value needed across steps in a process execution
Dynamic value; not the same as a configured component field.
Value associated with a specific document
Useful for document-specific metadata and routing.
Connector-specific setting such as file name or directory
Often set through Set Properties before a connector step.
Environment-specific overrides for supported process settings
Same process design can use different endpoint/credential values in different environments.

cert06.text: Use extensions where the process is intended to be promoted with environment-specific configuration. Validate the effective values at deployment and during Test Mode. Do not hard-code Production credentials in a shared process component.
A process works in Test but fails in Production: compare endpoint, folder, credentials, certificates, network route and extension values.
A shared connection is changed and several integrations fail: identify all component dependencies and consider a separate component or controlled version.
A property seems unchanged: check whether the correct property type and scope were selected, whether a persistent property or extension overrides it, and where the value is set.

cert07.text: Test Mode is not the same as a Test environment

Test Mode runs a process from the Build page without deploying it to a runtime environment. It gives step-level feedback and is useful during development. A Test environment is an environment to which a process can be deployed and exercised as an integration release.
Safety: Test Mode executes real configured actions. Data can be read, created, modified or deleted. Use test systems and safe sample data; never assume Test Mode is a harmless simulation.

head: Test class
Example
Expected evidence
rows: Valid customer with all required fields
Correct target payload and successful send
Maximum length, zero, large number, optional field absent
Invalid date, malformed JSON, missing required ID
Clear failure or controlled reject route
Expired password or unreachable endpoint in a safe test system
Meaningful connection error and recovery action
Expected document count and acceptable behavior
Test extension values and deployed Test process
Correct Test endpoint, credentials and output

cert07.text: Find the execution in Process Reporting and confirm process, runtime, timestamp, execution mode and status.
Open execution details and identify the failing connection, document or shape.
Read the process and document logs; locate the first meaningful error, not just the final cascade.
Inspect the inbound document and the data immediately before the failing step.
Check the connector connection, operation, profile, permissions, network and extension values.
Reproduce with a small safe input in Test Mode or a Test environment.
Fix the root cause, rerun the failed document where supported, and verify the target-side result.
Record cause, correction, evidence and prevention.

Current official Process Reporting documentation states that logs are retained for 30 days by default, and that Test Mode executions can appear in reporting but their documents and logs are not available there. Test Mode logs/data are temporary and are lost when exiting Test Mode. Confirm current account retention and archiving options.

cert09.text: Connector names and capabilities may vary by account, connector version and platform release. The current official documentation should be used for exact fields and authentication choices. The original Activities 6 and 7 provide the preserved FTP and Disk setup walkthroughs.
Authentication failure: verify credential validity, token scope, certificate and account permissions.
Timeout: verify endpoint health, DNS, firewall, proxy, port, response time and connector timeout settings.
File not found: check remote/local path, case sensitivity, wildcard, file permissions and runtime machine.
Database error: check JDBC driver, network route, schema, SQL, data types and transaction constraints.
Unexpected response: compare actual payload to operation profile and inspect HTTP status or application error body.

cert10.text: 9. Hands-on certification practice path

Complete the original 20 activities first. Then use the following independent-build challenge. The challenge intentionally combines the same core competencies in a fresh business scenario so that success does not depend on memorizing screenshots.
Capstone: supplier product feed to inventory API

Scenario: A supplier drops a delimited file on SFTP each morning. The file contains SKU, Description, UnitPrice, Quantity and Status. The target inventory API expects JSON with sku, description, price, availableQuantity and active.
Input example

SKU-1001,Desk Lamp,29.95,18,ACTIVE
SKU-1002,Chair,89.00,0,INACTIVE
Expected target example
{"sku":"SKU-1001","description":"Desk Lamp","price":29.95,"availableQuantity":18,"active":true}
Build steps
Create a clearly named folder for the capstone and separate connection components.
Configure an SFTP connection and Get operation using a non-production endpoint and a narrow file filter.
Import or manually create a Flat File profile; verify delimiter, header handling, field names and data types.
Create a JSON destination profile matching the target API contract.
Create a process with an SFTP Start connector, a Map and an HTTP Client Send connector.
Map fields; convert UnitPrice and Quantity to numeric target types; convert Status to the required Boolean rule.
Add validation for missing SKU, invalid price, negative quantity and unsupported status.
Use a reject/error route or exception strategy that preserves the original SKU and reason.
Test one valid row, multiple rows, blank fields, malformed numbers and a file with an extra delimiter.
Package the process, deploy to Test, set endpoint and credentials using environment configuration, then execute.
Verify Process Reporting and the target API response; document the execution ID and test evidence.
Promote the same packaged version to Production only after controlled approval and extension verification.
Acceptance criteria
Valid rows produce JSON that matches the target contract.
Invalid rows are identified with a useful reason and are not silently dropped.
A failed target call is visible in logs/reporting and can be investigated.
Environment-specific host and credentials are not hard-coded.
The deployed version and final test evidence are recorded.
Additional mini-labs

Pass condition
rows: Set output filename from a document value and use an environment-specific folder
Correct file name per document; correct folder per environment

Send an employee record to two independent test destinations
Both intended paths receive the document
Map XML customer data to flat file with one default
Intentionally break a test credential, profile or path
Identify first failing step and root cause from evidence

Conditional route; fan-out to multiple paths.
Build-time test execution; deployed environment used for integration testing.

Per-document context; process execution-level runtime value.
Configured reusable process value; environment-specific override for supported settings.

cert13.text: The following questions are original practice questions written for this book. They are not real or recalled examination questions and are not represented as official exam items. Choose the best answer before reading the explanation. Questions cover associate-level process development competencies and practical reasoning.

Suggested self-assessment: 1 point per question. A score is useful only when combined with hands-on evidence. For the scenario items, write down the first diagnostic action and the evidence you would inspect.

items.q: Which Boomi object executes a deployed process?
items.e: A Component Explorer organizes reusable components. A profile describes data structure, and a map defines transformation. The runtime executes deployed processes.

items.q: Which statement best distinguishes a connector, connection and operation?
o: Connector is the endpoint; connection is the action; operation is the adapter
Connector is the adapter type; connection stores endpoint/access settings; operation defines the action
They are three names for the same object
items.e: The connector identifies the technology/application; the connection contains endpoint/access details; the operation specifies the action and request/response behavior.

items.q: What is the primary purpose of a profile?
o: To describe the structure or format of a document
items.e: Profiles describe data layout. Maps transform between profiles; deployment and authentication are separate concerns.

items.q: A source file contains 50 customer rows. What should you avoid assuming?
o: The file may contain multiple records
One file must always equal one business record
A profile can describe its structure
items.e: A document is the processing unit, but it can contain multiple records. Splitting or processing can change document count.

items.q: Which shape is best for mutually exclusive true/false routing?
items.e: Decision evaluates a condition and routes accordingly. Branch fans out into multiple paths.

items.q: Which shape is appropriate when the same document must go to two independent downstream systems?
items.e: Branch provides fan-out. A Decision chooses one conditional route.

items.q: Where should an environment-specific endpoint be configured when extensions are supported?
items.e: Extensions allow supported settings to vary by deployment environment while preserving the process design.

items.q: What is a Dynamic Document Property most suited to?
o: Storing context associated with a particular document
items.e: Dynamic Document Properties carry document-specific runtime values. They differ from Dynamic Process Properties.

items.q: Which statement about Test Mode is safest?
o: It executes the configured process and can perform real actions
It is identical to deploying to Production
items.e: Test Mode executes actual configured actions. Use safe test systems and data.

items.q: Where do you normally investigate a deployed execution and its logs?
items.e: Process Reporting is the operational view for executions and related document/log information, subject to retention and availability.

items.q: A process fails at the HTTP Send connector. What is the best first diagnostic approach?
o: Inspect the failing step, error detail, endpoint/authentication and request payload
items.e: Start with the failing step and first meaningful error, then verify endpoint, credentials, request profile and actual payload.

items.q: What does a Map component primarily do?
o: Transform data from source structure to destination structure
Attach a runtime to an environment
items.e: A Map defines field mappings and functions between source and destination profiles.

items.q: A target field is mandatory but the source may omit it. What is the best design decision?
o: Guess a value in every case
Define a business-approved default or reject the document
items.e: A default must reflect an agreed business rule. Otherwise reject or route invalid data rather than inventing values.

items.q: What is the most important risk when editing a shared connection component?
o: It changes only the currently open process
It may affect other processes that reuse it
It changes the profile schema automatically
items.e: Components are reusable. Check dependencies before modifying shared components.

items.q: Which is the correct release sequence?
items.e: Build changes design; package creates a versioned release; deploy installs it; execute runs it; monitor verifies results.

items.q: A Disk connector points to a path that exists on a developer laptop, but the process runs on a remote runtime. What is likely wrong?
o: Disk paths are evaluated on the runtime machine
The Map has to be renamed
items.e: The runtime accesses its own filesystem and reachable paths, not automatically the developer's local disk.

items.q: Which data should be used to validate a flat-file profile?
o: Representative sample files including edge cases
A screenshot of the canvas only
items.e: The profile must match real delimiters, qualifiers, headers, field order and data types.

items.q: What is a likely cause of a mapping conversion failure?
o: Source value format does not match the target type or conversion expectation
Process folder has a descriptive name
The process has a Stop shape
items.e: Inspect the source value, data type, date/number format and map function configuration.

items.q: Which best describes an Operation component?
o: It defines a specific action against the endpoint, such as Get or Query
It is a document tracking field
items.e: The operation configures the action and often the request/response profile.

items.q: A customer has no email. The business rule says such records must not reach ERP. What should you build?
o: A Branch to send it to ERP anyway
A Decision or validation route to a reject path
items.e: Use a condition to separate valid and invalid documents and preserve rejection details.

items.q: Which is the safest approach to a production deployment?
o: Use developer credentials in the process
Verify package version, target environment, extensions and smoke test
Assume Test success guarantees Production success
items.e: A controlled release checks version, environment configuration, connectivity and post-deployment evidence.

items.q: Why is a profile re-import worth checking against dependent maps?
o: It may change field paths or structure references
items.e: Profile structure changes can affect mappings that reference the old elements.

items.q: What is the main role of a Process Property component?
o: Provide configured reusable property values for a process
items.e: Process Property components define process-level configured values; dynamic properties and extensions have different roles.

items.q: A process completes but a business record is missing at the target. What should you verify?
o: Document counts, routing, errors, target response and business-level success
items.e: A top-level execution status may not prove every business record was delivered as intended.

items.q: Which statement about Process Reporting retention should be treated carefully?
o: Current documentation says logs are retained 30 days by default; verify account settings
Reports are stored in the Map component
items.e: The official Process Reporting page describes a 30-day default log retention. Check current account configuration and archiving needs.

items.q: What should you do if Test Mode reports a successful run but you need durable production evidence?
o: Assume the Test Mode log is permanent
Deploy to the appropriate test environment and review deployed execution reporting
Use only a screenshot of the canvas
items.e: Test Mode data is temporary and differs from deployed execution reporting. Use environment testing for release evidence.

items.q: A process uses Branch to send one employee record to Payroll and Identity. One branch fails. What is important?
o: Confirm how errors on each path are handled and reported
items.e: Fan-out introduces multiple downstream outcomes. Design and verify error handling and observability for each path.

items.q: What is a connection component most likely to contain?
items.e: Connection components hold endpoint and access configuration.

items.q: Which action is appropriate when the same packaged process is promoted from Test to Production?
o: Apply the Production extension values and verify runtime/environment
items.e: The same design can be deployed with environment-specific settings where supported.

items.q: What does the Start step represent?
o: The entry point for a process
items.e: Start is the process entry step and commonly defines the inbound trigger or connector.

items.q: Which is a good first check for an SFTP connection failure?
o: Verify host, port, credentials or key, host key and network reachability
items.e: SFTP failures commonly relate to authentication, host key, network route, port or permissions.

items.q: Which input condition is different from an empty string?
items.e: A missing field is absent from the structure; an empty string exists but has no characters.

items.q: A target API rejects a request with a schema error. What should you compare?
o: Actual outbound payload against the operation's request profile and API contract
items.e: Application connector operations expect data matching the request profile and target contract.

items.q: What is the purpose of packaging?
o: Create a versioned snapshot for release
items.e: Packaging creates a versioned component snapshot used in deployment.

items.q: What does undeployment do?
o: Remove a deployed process from an environment/runtime
items.e: Undeployment removes the deployed instance; consider schedules, listeners and operational impact.

items.q: Which statement about Branch is most accurate?
o: It evaluates one condition and chooses true/false
It creates multiple execution paths for the document
items.e: Branch is used for fan-out to multiple paths.

items.q: Why should you test with malformed and boundary data?
o: To prove only the happy path works
To reveal validation, conversion and routing weaknesses
items.e: Robust tests cover expected, boundary and negative cases.

items.q: An execution fails after a password rotation. Which configuration should be checked first?
o: The relevant connection or extension credential
items.e: Credential rotation commonly breaks connection authentication; verify the actual effective runtime value.

items.q: What is the key distinction between a process and a runtime?
o: A process defines steps; a runtime executes deployed processes
A process stores host credentials; runtime stores maps
items.e: The process is design; runtime is execution infrastructure.

items.q: Which is a sensible validation strategy for a required numeric price?
o: Validate presence and numeric format; route invalid values explicitly
Default all prices to 0 without approval
items.e: Validate required fields and conversion before target delivery; defaults must be business-approved.

items.q: A file contains commas inside quoted descriptions. What should you verify?
o: Flat File profile delimiter and text qualifier settings
items.e: Delimiter and qualifier settings control how fields are parsed when delimiters appear inside quoted values.

items.q: Which is the strongest evidence that an integration worked?
o: The execution completed and target-side data/results were verified
The package has a version number
items.e: Operational success includes execution evidence and confirmation that the target accepted the intended business data.

items.title: Scenario 1. A nightly SFTP feed is empty, but the process reports success. What do you inspect?
items.model: Review the inbound operation filter and file pattern, source directory, schedule and whether zero inbound documents are considered a successful no-op. Confirm runtime access and inspect the execution details. Do not assume success means the expected file was found.
items.concept: Diagnose from evidence at the first point where expected behavior diverges; do not make broad changes before isolating the cause.

items.title: Scenario 2. A Map fails only when a date field is blank. What do you do?
items.model: Inspect the actual source value and profile; distinguish missing, null and empty; check the date conversion function and target requirement; add an explicit default or reject route only if the business rule allows it; test blank and valid dates.
items.concept: Diagnose from evidence at the first point where expected behavior diverges; do not make broad changes before isolating the cause.

items.title: Scenario 3. A process works in Test but fails in Production. Give a diagnostic order.
items.model: Compare deployed package/version, Production extension values, endpoint and credentials, certificate, runtime attachment/network reachability, firewall/proxy, target permissions, and production data differences. Use Process Reporting to identify the first failing step.
items.concept: Diagnose from evidence at the first point where expected behavior diverges; do not make broad changes before isolating the cause.

items.title: Scenario 4. One document is sent to the ERP twice after a retry. What do you investigate?
items.model: Check retry scope and idempotency behavior, whether the first send succeeded but the response was lost, document identity/business key, target upsert support, and whether the retry replays the same transaction. Add safe duplicate prevention based on business requirements.
items.concept: Diagnose from evidence at the first point where expected behavior diverges; do not make broad changes before isolating the cause.

items.title: Scenario 5. A Branch sends to two targets; one target is down. What design questions matter?
items.model: Decide whether both targets are mandatory, whether one path can succeed independently, how branch errors are captured, whether partial success is acceptable, and how replay avoids duplicates. Make failure visible and define a controlled recovery.
items.concept: Diagnose from evidence at the first point where expected behavior diverges; do not make broad changes before isolating the cause.

items.title: Scenario 6. A connector receives an unexpected response structure. What do you verify?
items.model: Compare actual response payload with the operation response profile, endpoint/version, request parameters and headers. Confirm whether the API returned an error body or different content type. Update profile/map only after validating the actual contract.
items.concept: Diagnose from evidence at the first point where expected behavior diverges; do not make broad changes before isolating the cause.

items.title: Scenario 7. You change a shared connection and three processes break. What lesson and recovery?
items.model: A reusable component change affects all dependents. Restore the previous known-good configuration or create a separate connection, inspect dependencies, test each consumer and deploy controlled versions. Document ownership and change impact.
items.concept: Diagnose from evidence at the first point where expected behavior diverges; do not make broad changes before isolating the cause.

items.title: Scenario 8. A file has 10,000 rows but only 1,000 documents appear downstream. What do you inspect?
items.model: Determine whether the connector reads multiple files, whether profile parsing and split settings produce record-level documents, whether Data Process or filters reduce count, and whether errors/reject paths account for missing records. Trace counts at each shape.
items.concept: Diagnose from evidence at the first point where expected behavior diverges; do not make broad changes before isolating the cause.

head: Domain
Score 0-4
Evidence required
rows: Explain platform, runtime, environment, component and deployment relationships.
Configure at least two connector types and explain connection vs operation.
Build a transformation with valid, missing and invalid fields.
Trace document counts and explain document/process property scope.
Use Decision and Branch correctly; explain exception handling.
Find root cause for three deliberately introduced failures.
Package, deploy, execute and verify an integration in Test.

cert15.text: Scoring: 0 = cannot explain; 1 = recognizes terms but cannot perform; 2 = performs with notes/help; 3 = performs independently and explains why; 4 = handles edge cases and troubleshoots independently.

Suggested readiness gate (a study recommendation, not an official Boomi passing score): average at least 3/4 in every domain, complete the capstone without step-by-step instructions, and score at least 85% on two fresh practice sets while explaining every missed answer. Any domain below 3 requires targeted practice before booking.
I completed all 20 preserved original activities in order.
I can create a process from a blank canvas and configure connectors, connections and operations.
I can explain and create XML, JSON and flat-file profiles.
I can build a Map and test conversions, defaults, nulls and invalid values.
I can explain document flow and predict how shape behavior changes document counts.
I can choose Decision or Branch based on the business requirement.
I can distinguish Dynamic Document Properties, Dynamic Process Properties, Process Properties and Extensions.
I can test safely and explain the limitations of Test Mode.
I can inspect Process Reporting, execution logs and document-level failures.
I can package, deploy, execute, monitor and undeploy a process.
I can troubleshoot a failed connector, mapping, property or deployment without random edits.
I checked the current exam details and prerequisites in the official learner portal.

Book only when the evidence above is met and you have verified current registration rules, prerequisites, format, schedule, retake policy and any exam-specific instructions in the official Boomi Training and Certification portal. Do not infer these from old forum posts or third-party course outlines.

cert16.text: Boomi's UI labels, connector versions, product packaging and runtime terminology can change. This book intentionally uses concepts that remain useful across UI changes and directs the learner to official current documentation for exact field names.

The original source book contains classic terms such as Atom, Molecule and Atom Cloud alongside newer Runtime wording, and notes that menu labels may vary. Preserve that context when studying, but use the names displayed in the current account.

Some process steps and capabilities are edition-dependent. Official process-step documentation identifies certain advanced workflow features as available only in Professional and Enterprise editions. Verify account entitlements before planning an exercise around a feature.

Test Mode details and Process Reporting retention are version-sensitive. The official documentation reviewed for this edition states that Test Mode can perform real actions, has execution limits, and produces temporary logs/data; Process Reporting documents a 30-day default log retention. These are current documentation statements, not a guarantee of every account's configuration.

This supplement is additional certification coaching, not a replacement for the original book. The source portion retains its theory, practical activities, screenshots, examples, diagrams, glossary, interview questions, troubleshooting matrix and cheat sheets. The duplicate original indexes and final standalone legal page were omitted and replaced with one new unified clickable index. No claim is made that original August 2026 training screenshots have been revalidated against every current tenant UI.
